Forty-four comments

New Mown Meadows

A great reel, and reputedly a close cousin of “The Silver Spear”. Sometimes played half an octave lower, but I think this is the more common version nowadays. Seems popular on all instruments, as it’s been recorded by Sean Keane, Kevin Burke, Noel Hill and Brian Hughes, to name just 4.

↳ Posted by Kenny on March 23rd, 2004.

Threepenny Bit

This was “The Threepenny Bit” to Francis O’Neill. It’s played in more than one key.

↳ Posted by blarneystar on March 26th, 2004.

Might be more common in this key in your area, Kenny, but I only ever hear it in Edor.

↳ Posted by Dr. Dow on July 24th, 2006.

Ador/Edor ?

Ador / Edor - I’m not too much bothered, one way or the other, Dow. As for how it’s played in “my area”, at a guess there are only another 2 or possibly 3 musicians within a 50 mile radius who play it at all.
I’m able to check through 10 or so of the recordings listed - I’ll get back to you about what keys they play the tune in, just out of interest.

The New Mown Meadows, X:14

Sliabh Luachra version, starting on a long A. Ties omitted. This setting is from Dan Herlihy’s 2003 publication of manuscripts given to Padraig O‘Keeffe’s pupils (page 37 tune 2). The reel had no name. Lack of repeat signs does not imply it is played as a single reel, as recordings of POK et al. testify: https://thesession.org/recordings/519?tune_id=2706 . Johnny O’Leary has a similar setting (which is close to Kenny’s X:1) in his book (#152)

↳ Posted by brailsford on December 6th, 2021.

The New Mown Meadows, X:15

Here’s the singled, D minor to G major version I referenced years ago as played by Marty O’Keefe under the name “Mick Clune’s.” In addition to the unusual singled structure, the ending that focuses more on a repeated G gives it a different feel from a lot of the other settings posted.
